author: Brian Weckerly
title: Trump administration to end subsidies for Medicare - NewsBreak
text:
By Brian Weckerly ,
1 hours ago
Plans from the Trump administration will end federal subsidies that help pay for Medicare .
The administration claims the subsidies benefit insurance companies more than enrollees.
The subsidies for Medicare Part D established during the Biden administration expire at the end of the year and will not be offered next year. Medicare Part D is optional prescription drug coverage offered by private insurance companies to help people with Medicare pay for brand-name and generic medication. The program was restructured to implement a $2,000 annual cap on out-of-pocket spending on prescription drugs. It also let Medicare negotiate prices for some expensive drugs.
Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa says he wants to change the rules for pharmacy benefit managers, blaming them for rising costs. Grassley is part of the bipartisan effort with Oregon senator Ron Wyden to lower drug costs and make health care more affordable.
About 25 million Americans carry standalone Medicare Part D drug plans.
